newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cyprus president ready for talks after preparations.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus president ready for talks after preparations.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides said on Thursday he was ready to hold face-to-face talks with Turkish Cypriots next year on ending the division of the island if there are preparations first sufficient to ensure success.
"We are prepared to embark on face-to-face negotiations in 1997 once the ground has been sufficiently prepared to ensure success," Clerides said.

"We are not, however, willing after 22 years of negotiations, which have not yielded any result on the main issues of the problem, to embark on another round of fruitless talks," he said in a speech to the General Assembly.

That would destroy the credibility of the negotiating process while keeping the attention of the international community focused on the intercommunal aspect of the problem, he said, "thus overshadowing the real issue which is the invasion and continued occupation for 22 years of substantial territory of the Republic of Cyprus by the Turkish forces."
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since Turkish troops landed in the north in 1974 after a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.

The United Nations has tried for decades to reunite the Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots under a federal system. The last face-to-face negotiations at U.N. headquarters between Clerides, as leader of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash took place in 1993.
They held informal meetings in Nicosia the following year under U.N. auspices but failed to agree on terms for a full-scale resumption of negotiations.
Denktash, president of a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state recognised only by Turkey, has said he was ready for talks.

Clerides repeated a longstanding proposal to demilitarize Cyprus, including disbanding the National Guard and handing over weapons to an international force, in exchange for the withdrawal of all foreign troops -- a reference to the estimated 35,000 Turkish troops in the north of the island.

He said the urgent need to implement this proposal was highlighted by the recent "brutal killings of two Greek Cypriot unarmed demonstrators ... by the Turkish occupation troops and Turkish extremists imported from mainland Turkey to the occupied part of the island."

He expressed sorrow for "a subsequent killing of a Turkish soldier and the wounding of another" but regretted what he called the haste with which Denktash "attempted to attribute responsibility for this killing to the Greek Cypriot side" before an independent U.N. investigation was completed.
